report:
Pancreas and duodenum, head of pancreas, pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple resection)

Received in formalin is a pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple resection) specimen measuring 150 x 90 x 60 mm. The pancreatic head measures 55 x 45 x 35 mm, the attached duodenum measures 160 mm in length and the common bile duct measures 35 mm in length. The pancreatic neck, bile duct, uncinate (superior mesenteric artery) and posterior surfaces are inked in different colours and the neck and bile duct margins are taken en face. There is a firm, ill-defined pale tumour centred on the head of pancreas measuring 32 x 28 x 20 mm. The pancreatic duct is dilated to 6 mm upstream and the common bile duct is dilated to 14 mm. The lymph node stations are dissected separately and submitted in labelled cassettes. Representative sections are taken; see block key.

(1-4) Tumour with posterior surface.
(5) Pancreatic neck margin, en face.
(6) Bile duct margin, en face.

Specimen and tumour
- Procedure: Pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple resection)
- Origin: Pancreatic (ductal adenocarcinoma centred in the pancreatic head or
  uncinate process)
- Tumour site: Head of pancreas
- Tumour size: 3.2 cm (unifocal invasive carcinoma, greatest dimension)

Microscopic findings
- Histologic type: Ductal adenocarcinoma, NOS
- Histologic grade: G2, moderately differentiated
- Tumour histology:
  The tumour is a moderately differentiated ductal adenocarcinoma, NOS, extending into the peripancreatic soft tissue and duodenal wall. Haphazardly arranged infiltrating glands with incomplete lumina and luminal necrotic debris are set in abundant desmoplastic stroma, lying immediately adjacent to muscular vessels and nerves, and show marked variation in nuclear size within individual glands. The tumour cells express CK7. There is loss of nuclear SMAD4 (DPC4) expression.
- Sites involved by direct extension: Peripancreatic soft tissue and Duodenal
  wall
- Pancreatic surface involvement: Posterior surface involved
- Lymphovascular invasion: Present
- Perineural invasion: Present
- Treatment effect: No known presurgical therapy
- Precursor lesion: Pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia, high grade (PanIN)

Margins
- Pancreatic neck (transection) margin: Uninvolved by invasive carcinoma, 8 mm
- Bile duct margin: Uninvolved by invasive carcinoma, 12 mm
- Uncinate (retroperitoneal / superior mesenteric artery) margin: Uninvolved by
  invasive carcinoma, 0.8 mm
- Posterior surface: Involved by invasive carcinoma
- Proximal (gastric or duodenal) margin: Uninvolved by invasive carcinoma, 45 mm
- Distal (duodenal or jejunal) margin: Uninvolved by invasive carcinoma, 60 mm
- High-grade dysplasia at the margins: Not identified

Lymph nodes
- Regional lymph nodes: 18 examined; 3 involved
  - Number examined: 18
  - Number involved: 3
  - Stations involved: 13 (posterior pancreaticoduodenal): 2 and 17 (anterior
    pancreaticoduodenal): 1
  - Extranodal extension: Not identified
  - Size of largest metastatic deposit: 6 mm, station 13

Distant metastasis
- Distant metastasis: Not identified

Pathological stage (AJCC 8th edition)
- pTNM: pT2 pN1
  - Stage group (if cM0): IIB

Additional findings
- Chronic pancreatitis

PANCREAS AND DUODENUM, head of pancreas, pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple
resection)
- DUCTAL ADENOCARCINOMA, NOS, moderately differentiated, 3.2 cm, extending into
  the peripancreatic soft tissue and duodenal wall; lymphovascular invasion
  present; perineural invasion present; posterior surface involved; uncinate
  margin 0.8 mm (margin positive at 1 mm or less); remaining margins clear
  (closest 8 mm); see synoptic report
- 3 of 18 regional lymph nodes involved
- pT2 pN1 (AJCC 8th edition), stage IIB (if cM0)

checks.message: Extrapancreatic extension is recorded with a tumour of 4 cm or less. In the eighth edition pT follows size alone, so this remains pT1 or pT2; extension no longer raises it to pT3.
Uncinate (retroperitoneal / superior mesenteric artery) margin is 0.8 mm from the carcinoma; at 1 mm or less this is reported as a positive margin (R1) in pancreatobiliary resections.
